info.name: Crumb & Co. — Customer Only
info.description:
Customer-only flows for the Crumb & Co. e-commerce backend (Express v5 + Prisma).

## Setup
1. Start the server: `npm run dev` (defaults to http://localhost:4000).
2. Seed the database: `npm run db:seed` (creates the admin and products — the catalog reads below use the seeded product `classic-chocolate-chip`).
3. Import the environment `crumb-and-co.environment.json` and select it.

## How to run
- Run the whole collection in order (Auth → Me → Catalog → Cart → Orders → Negative Tests → Cleanup).
- Auth > Login Customer captures the JWT into `accessToken`; every customer request reads it via `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}`.
- Logout runs last (in Cleanup) so the token stays valid for all the customer requests and negative tests.
- Re-running is mostly idempotent: Register tolerates 409 (already exists). The final rate-limit test locks /auth/login + /auth/refresh for ~1 minute, so it runs last.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Register + login the customer. The customer JWT is stored to `accessToken`, used by every customer request in this collection.

exec: pm.test('201 on first run (409 if email already registered)', () => pm.expect([201, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code));

item.name: Register Managed User
item.description: Second account used by the 'Update Me — email already in use' negative test. On re-runs this 409s (already registered), which is fine.

exec: pm.test('201 on first run (409 if already registered)', () => pm.expect([201, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code));

item.name: Login Customer
item.description: Stores the JWT in `accessToken` and the user id in `customerUserId`.

item.name: Refresh
item.description: Reads the httpOnly `refreshToken` cookie automatically. Rotates the session and returns a fresh access token.

item.name: Me
item.description: Current authenticated customer profile. Requires `accessToken` (set by Auth > Login Customer).

item.name: Get Me
item.description: Requires a valid access token. Run 'Auth > Login Customer' first — it stores the JWT in `accessToken`, which this request sends as `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}`.

exec: throw new Error('accessToken is empty — run "Auth > Login Customer" first (and make sure the "Crumb & Co. — Local" environment is selected).');

item.name: Catalog (public reads)
item.description: Products are public to read - no token needed. 'Get Product by Slug' captures the product id used by the cart and orders flows.

item.name: Get Product by Slug
item.description: Uses a seeded product and captures its id for the cart/checkout flow.

item.name: Cart
item.description: Per-user cart. The last request re-adds an item so the cart-based checkout in the Orders folder has stock to buy.

item.name: Orders
item.description: Checkout (guest and cart-based), listing and single order. Mock payment auto-pays, so orders are created as PAID.

item.name: Checkout (cart)
item.description: Authenticated checkout without `items` uses the user's cart and clears it after.

item.name: Checkout (guest)
item.description: Guest checkout sends explicit items. Saves the guest order id for the 403 negative test.

item.name: Negative Tests (Customer)
item.description: Failure scenarios for customer/auth routes (400/401/403/404/409/429). Runs after the happy paths so it can reuse captured ids and the customer token. The final rate-limit test temporarily locks /auth/login + /auth/refresh for ~1 minute.

item.name: Refresh — without cookie (401)
item.description: Clears the cookie jar first so the refresh token cookie is gone → 'Missing refresh token'.

item.name: List Users — customer token (403)
item.description: Customer token hitting an admin-only route.

item.name: Get Guest Order as Customer (403)
item.description: A customer trying to view an order that belongs to no one (guest) or another user → forbidden.

item.name: Update Order Status as Customer (403)
item.description: A customer trying to update an order status (admin-only action).

item.name: Get Order — not found (404)
item.description: A valid UUID that does not exist.

item.name: Add Cart Item — invalid product id (400)
Add Cart Item — product not found (404)
item.description: Valid UUID but the product does not exist.

item.name: Update Cart Item — not in cart (404)
item.description: The product is not in the customer's cart.

item.name: Remove Cart Item — not in cart (404)
Checkout — nonexistent product (400 / NOT_FOUND)
item.description: Checkout with a product that does not exist returns HTTP 400 with code NOT_FOUND.

item.name: Checkout — empty cart (409)
item.description: Authenticated checkout without items while the cart is empty → conflict. (Cart was cleared by the happy-path checkout.)

item.name: Update Me — email already in use (409)
item.description: Tries to change the customer's email to another existing user's email (the managed user).

item.name: Login — rate limited (429)
item.description: Fires 6 rapid login attempts in the pre-request script to exhaust the auth limiter (5/min), then this login should be blocked. Note: this test locks out /auth/login and /auth/refresh for about a minute, so it runs last.

exec: body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ email: pm.environment.get('customerEmail'), password: 'wrong' }) }

item.name: Cleanup
item.description: Logs the customer out. Runs last so `accessToken` stays valid for every customer request and negative test above.
